comparisons.peer_topic: Risk to Compensation and Efficiency Ratio Targets
comparisons.peer_summary: Statements regarding future compensation expense levels and the efficiency ratio are subject to risk that compensation and other operating costs may exceed current expectations.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Goldman Sachs explicitly disclose compensation expense as a key financial metric and highlight the associated risks or components. BAC quantifies compensation and benefits expense at $40.2 billion (60% of noninterest expense), whereas GS focuses on the risk that 'compensation and other operating costs may be greater than currently expected' for future expense levels. While BAC provides historical absolute values and GS discusses forward-looking risk exposure to those same costs, both filings treat compensation expense as a material driver of operating costs.

sentences.text: Additionally, in 2024 and 2023, the Corporation's compensation and benefits expense was $40.2 billion and $38.3 billion, or 60 percent and 58 percent, of total noninterest expense.

Statements about the level of future compensation expense, including as a percentage of both operating expenses and net revenues, net of provision for credit losses, and our efficiency ratio are subject to the risks that the compensation and other costs to operate our businesses may be greater than currently expected.
